songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Epic 18‑minute Spanish Jam anchors a solid early‑Dead set
ai_show_review.blurb: The first set rolls through classic material and ends with an extended, cinematic Spanish Jam that runs close to twenty minutes. Jerry’s guitar roars while Phil’s bass is unusually forward in the mix, and the twin drums deliver a snappy, propulsive beat. The Miller soundboard capture offers clear, balanced audio making this jam shine.
ai_show_review.review: Seattle’s Eagle's Auditorium on January 27 1968 captured the Dead in an early‑period groove that still feels fresh. After navigating the familiar Cryptical/Other One sandwich, a handful of bluesy numbers and the Dark Star → China Cat Sunflower → The Eleven sequence, the band launches into an almost cinematic Spanish Jam. At nearly 18 minutes it becomes the show’s centerpiece: Jerry Garcia’s guitar erupts in “crazy, wicked” improvisations, Phil Lesh’s bass sits prominently forward, and both Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann lock into a tight, snappy rhythm that drives the music forward. The Miller soundboard tape (gd1968-01-27.sbd.miller.97344.sbeok.flac16) preserves this energy with clear separation, less tape wear than comparable sources, and a well‑balanced mix that highlights Phil’s low end while keeping the drums crisp. A second soundboard version exists but suffers from occasional feedback and a choppy texture that dulls some of Jerry’s lead tones. For anyone interested in hearing an early Dead jam at its most adventurous, this recording is the definitive choice.

best_recording.reason: Clearer tape with less wear, solid balance, prominent Phil mix and snappy drums make the Spanish Jam shine.

key_highlights: Extended 18‑minute Spanish Jam that feels cinematic
Jerry’s fiery, improvisational lead guitar throughout the jam
Phil Lesh’s bass sits unusually high in the mix, driving the groove
Snappy twin‑drum work from Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann adds propulsion

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers a fiery, improvisational lead during the Spanish Jam; occasional feedback in one source slightly muddies tone but overall his guitar is wild and compelling.
band_performance.Phil: Bass is front‑and‑center, thick and driving; both recordings note an unusually high mix that anchors the jam.
band_performance.Mickey: Provides tight, snappy drumming that propels the Spanish Jam forward.
band_performance.Billy: Locks in with Mickey for a crisp, energetic rhythm throughout the extended jam.
